newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, but seen moving up.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, but seen moving up.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.28 percent to end out the week 2.4 percent lower. Market participants said the fall was a reaction to steady growth since September and predicted shares would rebound.
They said strong interest of domestic and foreign investors in newly-privatised companies was expected to push up the index significantly in the next two and a half months.
"The index could gain up to 20 percent by the end of the year," one trader said. Since September 10, the SBI index has risen 42.2 percent.
* The SBI index eased 0.28 percent to 1,268.2.
* Turnover firmed to 461.6 million tolars from 329.4 million.
* 11 shares fell, five rose, one was steady and seven were untraded.
* Bank SKB had the highest turnover, falling 3.99 percent to 40,710 tolars on volume of 5,437 shares for total turnover of 225.5 million tolars.
* Preferred shares of bank Dolenjska bank were the leading decliners, falling 4.61 percent to 12,830 on volume of 65 shares for total turnover of 1.6 million tolars.

* Financial consultancy Primofin was the top gainer, rising 6.56 percent to 26,000 on volume of 100 shares for a total turnover of 2.6 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
